walkthrough: Goal: practise lines and colours the way I did on paper: copy a line, lay the original over my copy, correct in blue, compare again; for a colour, pick and fill beside the frame and see on the wheel where my pick lies against the original. No number for a line pretends to judge what my eye sees better.

Entry: a lesson of Lines at level 1 from the home. The sheet opens on Lines 1/6, its instructions on the card at the right (Got it closes them). The chrome holds only what lines use: Home and All tools at the top left, the practice bar in the middle; beside the empty frame at the right, the pens, Sketch (a light pencil) and Draw (chosen), and under them Undo and Redo. No side bar, no brush, layer or colour buttons: nothing else to look at, and nothing meets the bar in portrait.

Copy: I mark the line's two ends lightly with Sketch, choose Draw and draw the line in the empty frame, a little low and short. A stray stroke: Undo takes it back, Redo brings it, Undo again. Strokes stay in the frame; the pen's own samples are kept, no StreamLine.

Compare: the original lies over my copy in a thick, clear, semi-transparent red, in place: where it lies in its frame, so my placement errors show, as V大 checks. The card at the right reads Line 1 with In place and Aligned. One tap on Aligned: the red moves and sizes onto my line (never turned), so only the shape's errors show, however far off my placement was; one tap on In place brings it back. No numbers: the overlay is the feedback; my sketch marks are never judged and the aligned fit leaves them out.

Correct: after Compare the pen has turned blue: Correct is chosen beside the frame. As my pen lands in the frame the red and the card go, so I correct by eye; I draw the better line over the old one in blue. Compare again: the red comes back over the corrected copy in the mode I chose last. As often as I like; each Compare is counted, and every stroke after the first Compare is stored as a correction.

Next: the next pair glides in at my zoom; the pen is Draw again. On the sixth line Finish ends the lesson; That's all for today takes me home, and a lesson of Colours at level 1 opens on the next row of the same sheet.

Colours: on a colour the chrome holds, beside the empty frame at the right, the colour wheel and square (the colour panel's own) with the colour I am on and Fill frame. I pick by eye on the ring and in the square and tap Fill frame: the frame fills with it at once, no trip to the colour button. I compare by eye and pick and fill again.

Compare: each colour shows inside the other's frame, and the card shows the wheel with both colours placed, mine in ink and the original in red, with arrows from mine to it round the ring and across the square; under it the colour table: ΔE, then lightness, chroma and hue (Oklab's parts of ΔE, × 100), each a bar from the original's red line towards darker or lighter, greyer or purer, or the neighbouring hue mine lies towards, and its signed number; no sentence, and what ink and red mean is said once in How. The numbers kept are those of my first Compare: what my eye did before it saw the answer.

All tools: one tap at the top left brings the full interface onto the sheet (every island, the side bar, my own brushes and the colour button); All tools carries the ink pill. Tap it again: back to the exercise's own tools.

The end: Finish on the third colour shows the whole sheet; the card reads Colours, 3 exercises and the time, a dot for each result (the first ringed as the app judged it), the skill's dots, One more and That's all for today.

Levels (S141): a lesson of Lines at level 2 (熟练) holds an arc, an S, a hook and two meanders, lines that bend three times each way in turn, longer than the first level's: four or five key points to place instead of two or three. At level 3 (稳) meanders, a hook and three layered lines: a long arc or deep S carrying three to six small ripples, each about three pen widths from crest to trough; I place the big trend first, then the ripples on it (V大's W2 hierarchy). I copy one roughly and Compare: the red original lies over my line in place, its ripples plain beside my smooth stroke.
Not here: line numbers of any kind (a later study can measure the strokes kept); pen sizes or colours of my own on the practice pens (All tools has every brush).
